papers.title_en: Towards Probabilistically Safe Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Deployment on Humanoid and Aerial Robots
papers.authors: Pol Mestres, Varun Gabbita, Jason H. K. Siu, Sergio A. Esteban, Hampus Serneke, Joel W. Burdick, Aaron D. Ames
papers.evidence: 面向人形与空中机器人的安全强化学习控制
papers.tldr: 标准强化学习缺乏安全约束保证，现有可证明安全方法约束受限且依赖无偏估计，难以与PPO等先进算法结合。本文扩展RSGF-RL框架，支持一般轨迹级安全约束与机会约束，并允许有偏的值和梯度估计。理论证明训练中约束违反以高概率受估计偏差与随rollout增长而消失的项界定，迭代收敛到近似KKT点。基于PPO式估计实现Unitree G1全身控制与Crazyflie无碰撞导航的零样本仿真到现实部署。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables robots to acquire complex skills, but standard RL formulations do not guarantee that learned policies satisfy safety constraints, which limits their use in safety-critical settings. Existing safe RL methods with provable guarantees typically support only restricted classes of constraints and require unbiased estimators of the objective and constraint functions, which prevents their direct integration with state-of-the-art algorithms such as proximal policy optimization (PPO). In this paper, we extend the recently introduced robust safe gradient flow-based reinforcement learning (RSGF-RL) framework to overcome these limitations. Our formulation accommodates a general class of trajectory-level safety constraints, including chance constraints such as collision avoidance with a prescribed probability, and our analysis allows for biased value and gradient estimators. We show that, with high probability, the constraint violation throughout training is bounded by the estimator bias plus a term that vanishes as the number of rollouts grows, and decays to this level if the initial policy is unsafe. We also establish the convergence properties of the iterates to approximate KKT points of the original safe RL problem. Finally, we show that RSGF-RL implemented with PPO-style estimates enables zero-shot sim-to-real deployment of whole-body control policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid and collision-free waypoint navigation on a Crazyflie drone.

papers.title_en: Fuzzy Explainable Continual Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Navigation
papers.authors: Peng Qin, Tao Zhao
papers.evidence: 面向持续机器人导航的分层强化学习
papers.tldr: 面向持续机器人导航，强化学习需在新环境中持续适应并保留旧知识，但持续学习的策略稳定性与可解释行为学习所需的探索性存在冲突。本文提出模糊可解释持续分层强化学习FECHRL，用两阶段行为克隆从强模仿逐步过渡到自主强化学习，并引入基于Takagi-Sugeno模糊推理系统的模糊评论家缓解价值外推误差。多场景序贯导航实验表明，该方法能稳定保留知识并给出有意义的行为解释，将持续学习与策略可解释性统一于同一框架。
papers.abstract_en: Continual robot navigation requires reinforcement learning policies to continuously adapt to new environments while retaining previously acquired knowledge. Meanwhile, explainable reinforcement learning aims to learn meaningful behavioral representations through policy interaction. However, these objectives are inherently conflicting, as continual learning emphasizes policy stability whereas explainable behavior learning requires adaptive exploration. Existing methods rarely address both simultaneously. To resolve this issue, this paper proposes a Fuzzy Explainable Continual Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (FECHRL) method. A two-stage behavior cloning strategy is introduced to balance rapid policy adaptation and explainable behavior evolution by progressively transitioning from strong imitation guidance to autonomous reinforcement learning. Furthermore, a fuzzy critic based on a Takagi--Sugeno fuzzy inference system is proposed to alleviate value extrapolation errors during the transition between imitation-guided learning and autonomous exploration, thereby improving continual training stability. Experimental results on sequential multi-scenario navigation tasks demonstrate that the proposed method effectively unifies continual learning capability and policy explainability within a single reinforcement learning framework, achieving stable knowledge retention and meaningful behavioral explanation.

papers.title_en: Vision-Language Grounded Semantic Navigation for Autonomous Mobile Robots
papers.authors: Ravindran Vasoor Saravanan, Chittin Varunav Ravi, Madhumita Singh, Thirulok Sundar Mohan Rasu
papers.evidence: 用Grounding DINO进行开放词汇目标检测的机器人视觉导航
papers.tldr: 语言引导移动机器人需在非结构化环境理解自然语言并导航，但开放词汇视觉感知与经典建图导航流程难以整合。本文构建基于ROS2的完整系统，融合前沿探索、Grounding DINO开放词汇检测、深度三维定位与语义地图，并将检测目标转为Nav2导航目标。Gazebo中TurtleBot3自主探索房间，检出5个目标中的3个，并成功执行两项自然语言导航指令，无需任务特定训练。结果表明开放词汇grounding可接入经典导航管线，但受检测不确定性、深度定位误差和探索覆盖不足限制。
papers.abstract_en: Language-guided navigation enables mobile robots to interpret natural language commands and navigate toward user-specified targets in unstructured environments. However, integrating open-vocabulary visual perception with classical robotics pipelines for mapping and navigation remains a challenging problem. In this work, we present a complete ROS2-based system that combines frontier-based exploration, open-vocabulary object detection using Grounding DINO, depth-based 3D localization, and semantic mapping to enable end-to-end vision-language grounded navigation in simulation. The system accepts natural language commands such as ``go to the yellow box,'' detects candidate objects from RGB images using text prompts, estimates their positions in the world frame, and generates navigation goals executed by the Nav2 stack. In a Gazebo-based indoor environment with a TurtleBot3 robot, the system autonomously explored the room, detected three of the five target objects, and successfully executed both natural language navigation commands tested, without task-specific training. The results indicate that open-vocabulary grounding models can be integrated into classical navigation pipelines, though performance is limited by detection uncertainty, depth-based localization error, and incomplete exploration coverage. These findings highlight both the feasibility and current limitations of deploying vision-language grounded navigation systems using lightweight, CPU-only architectures.

papers.title_en: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
papers.authors: Ting-Hsuan Chen, Siheng Zhao, Han Jiang, Qi Pan, Louison Lu, Jiaheng Luo, Henghui Bao, Yiyu Chen, Quan Nguyen, Yue Wang
papers.evidence: 去中心化多 humanoid 协作与协调框架
papers.tldr: 人形机器人协作需全身交互、长程规划与精准同步，但去中心化执行困难。Heave-Ho低层用多智能体后训练适配人形基础跟踪模型，高层用视觉语言规划器与语音领导者-跟随者机制实现无网络通信协调。系统从双人训练扩展到十机团队，并泛化至异构团队；HH-Bench 12项任务上优于基线，真实实验验证鲁棒协作。为长程多机人形移动操作提供去中心化方案。
papers.abstract_en: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining. To benchmark these capabilities, we introduce HH-Bench, comprising 12 tasks involving teams of 2 to 10 humanoids, including heterogeneous teams. Systematic evaluations show that Heave-Ho consistently outperforms baseline methods, while real-world experiments demonstrate robust decentralized collaboration across challenging tasks.

papers.title_en: Embodied Interaction Policy: A Unified Model for Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction
papers.authors: Youqiang Gui, Yunfei Liu, Lijian Lin, Ye Zhu, Jianan Wang, Cheng Peng, Yu Li
papers.evidence: 统一的全双工人机社交交互策略
papers.tldr: 实时人机社交互动需要语音与动作连续协调，但现有系统将交互智能体与动作生成分离，难以随对话状态变化协同。EIP以分层联合注意力耦合音频交互专家与动作专家，并用分块因果掩码和发声token编码说话状态与情感。实验显示动作质量优于代表性手势基线，交互成功率更高，热启动延迟降低64%。该统一流式框架支持主动回应中的连续动作与打断感知轮转。
papers.abstract_en: Real-time human-robot social interaction requires continuous coordination between speech and physical behavior. Existing systems often separate interaction agents from motion generation, complicating coordination as conversational states change. We propose \textbf{Embodied Interaction Policy (EIP)}, a unified streaming framework that couples an Audio-Interaction expert with a motion expert through layer-wise joint attention. This allows motion generation to directly access the evolving interaction context. A chunk-wise causal mask prevents access to future context, while a vocal token encodes speaking state and the semantic emotion of the response. We construct \textbf{Embodied Interaction Dataset (EI-Data)} from co-speech and dyadic interaction data and train our model in two stages to learn state-adaptive and emotion-conditioned behavior. Combined with the frozen interaction expert, EIP supports continuous robot motion during proactive responses and interruption-aware turn-taking. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate improved motion quality over representative gesture-generation baselines. Compared with a representative cascaded system, EIP achieves higher interaction success and reduces warm-start latency by 64\%. Physical deployment and user studies further demonstrate improved motion naturalness and interaction comfort.

papers.title_en: MAWAM: Joint Imagination for Collaborative Robot Manipulation with a Multi-Agent World Action Model
papers.authors: Rongze Tang, Chenyu Zhou, Jianjie Fang, Ziming Liu, Zhaolu Wang, Ziyou Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Wei Wu, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Zhibo Chen
papers.evidence: 面向多机器人协同操作的多智能体世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 现有世界动作模型（WAM）擅长单机器人操作，却难以应对多机器人跨工作空间、时序耦合和异构本体协作。MAWAM将单智能体WAM沿智能体维度扩展，通过智能体轴课程与联合自注意力统一预测多本体未来观测并解码各自动作，同时用语言、身份编码和本体掩码绑定角色。在MA-Bench上，其平均联合成功率达82.7%，比最强基线高30.7个百分点，并在真实异构机器人团队上实现实时闭环协作。提出三轴问题形式化、MA-Task Harness与MA-Bench。
papers.abstract_en: World action models (WAMs) excel at robot manipulation by imagining future observations and decoding actions from them, yet remain confined to a single embodied agent. In practice, manipulation often requires multiple robots to collaborate across disjoint workspaces, coupled timing, and heterogeneous embodiments. Such coordination demands both spatiotemporal alignment of future interactions and awareness of individual embodiment and role identities, whereas existing decentralized per-robot policies, flat centralized models, and multi-robot VLAs fail to unite both. To bridge this gap, we present MAWAM, a multi-agent world action model that jointly predicts the future observations of multiple embodiments and decodes each agent's actions from them for collaborative manipulation. Through an agent-axis curriculum, MAWAM expands a single-agent WAM along an agent dimension to coordinate teams under shared weights. Within one unified causal sequence, joint self-attention spans all agents to spatiotemporally align their imagined futures, while hierarchical language, identity encodings, and embodiment masks bind each stream to its role, identity, and embodiment. We further formalize multi-agent-necessary manipulation along three axes (why, when, and who) and develop MA-Task Harness, a coding-agent pipeline where mutually constraining generators and evaluators co-evolve customizable simulation-data and evaluation packages. Using this pipeline, we build MA-Bench across all axes with seven tasks, pairing joint success rate with role and collaboration scores for fine-grained analysis. On MA-Bench, MAWAM reaches 82.7% mean joint success, 30.7% above the strongest baseline, and achieves real-time closed-loop collaboration on a real heterogeneous robot team.

papers.title_en: Dr. Grasp-RL: Diverse and Robust Dexterous Grasping via Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Kunqi Xu, Xiaokang Sun, Xueyan Zou
papers.evidence: 强化学习用于灵巧机器人抓取控制
papers.tldr: 灵巧抓取需兼顾多样策略与闭环鲁棒，但生成式方法多为开环执行，强化学习又易收敛到单一成功模式。本文提出时间反转课程与协同重置机制，使简单MLP策略经PPO训练即可覆盖抓取姿态分布的多模态并保持闭环控制。仅用约400个物体训练，在超2万个未见物体上展现多样抓取与强泛化。该工作统一了行为多样性与闭环鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Human interaction with physical objects relies on a combination of dexterity and robustness. In robotic manipulation, dexterity requires not only flexible end effectors but also a diverse repertoire of manipulation strategies, while robustness requires closed-loop adaptation to disturbances and unexpected situations. Two prominent research directions in dexterous grasping have largely addressed these capabilities separately. Generative approaches model multimodal distributions to produce diverse grasp poses, but their reliance on open-loop execution can limit robustness. Reinforcement learning approaches learn closed-loop grasping policies, but can converge to a narrow range of successful grasping strategies, limiting behavioral diversity. We introduce a time-reversed curriculum with a coordinated reset mechanism that enables a simple MLP policy trained with PPO to capture multiple modes of the grasp-pose distribution while maintaining closed-loop control. Experiments demonstrate both diverse grasping behaviors and robust closed-loop execution. Trained on only approximately 400 objects, our policy further demonstrates strong generalization when evaluated on more than 20,000 unseen objects.

papers.title_en: Seeing Together, Acting Apart: Shared Environmental Understanding for Multi-Robot Navigation
papers.authors: Haihong Hao, Lei Chen, Mingfei Han, Chenglong Yan, Dong An, Yuqiang Yang, Changlin Li, Minghao Guo, Salman Khan, Xiaojun Chang
papers.evidence: 多机器人共享环境理解与协作
papers.tldr: 多机器人具身系统通常通过协调动作、共享轨迹或联合策略实现协作，本文转而提出一个互补问题：协作能否在决策之前发生。作者提出共享环境理解（SEER），将各机器人的局部自我中心观测聚合为共享潜在世界模型，通过时空相似度检索相关上下文并以预测式潜在世界模型编码，作为 token 注入下游导航智能体。实验表明该方法能捕捉与动作相关的环境结构，在专用 VLN 智能体和通用视觉语言模型智能体上均稳定提升导航性能，同时保留单智能体能力。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-robot embodied systems are typically designed to collaborate by coordinating actions, sharing trajectories, or learning joint policies. We ask a complementary question: can collaboration emerge before decision-making, by first building a shared understanding of the environment? We introduce Shared Environmental Understanding, a policy-agnostic representation that aggregates partial egocentric observations from multiple robots into a shared latent world model. This shifts collaboration from the policy space to the representation space, enabling decentralized decision-making with shared environmental context. To this end, we propose Shared Environment Encoding and Retrieval (SEER), a framework that organizes multi-robot observations into a shared memory, retrieves relevant context via spatio-temporal similarity, and encodes it using a predictive latent world model. The resulting representations are injected into downstream navigation agents as tokens. Experimental results demonstrate that SEER captures action-relevant environmental structure and consistently improves navigation performance across both specialized VLN agents and general vision-language model agents, while preserving single-agent capabilities.

papers.title_en: OVOGO: Offline Value-Guided On-Policy Generative Optimization for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Rongzheng Yang, Jiaming Guo, Yuxuan Guo, Zihao Zhang, Yunkai Gao, Siming Lan, Shaohui Peng, Rui Zhang, Tianyun Ma, Xing Hu, Yunji Chen
papers.evidence: 面向流式视觉语言动作策略的离线强化学习
papers.tldr: 基于流的视觉-语言-动作模型可利用部署经验，但反复采集物理交互代价高。OVOGO将离线价值学习与生成过程的在线策略优化分离，用Return-Anchored Ranking Critic在保持日志经验约束的同时为新生动作提供价值信号。在RoboTwin 2.0、DexJoCo、LIBERO及真实机器人灵巧操作任务上，它均提升初始VLA并超过离线适应与价值引导基线。结果表明离线经验可重复用于价值学习，廉价生成采样足以支撑策略优化。
papers.abstract_en: Flow-based vision-language-action models can benefit from robot experience collected during deployment, but repeatedly acquiring new physical interactions for policy improvement is costly. Offline reinforcement learning provides a natural way to reuse collected experience, while flow-based policies offer an additional opportunity because fresh generation trajectories can be cheaply resampled from the current policy at replay observations. This motivates separating offline value learning from on-policy optimization of the generative process. We propose OVOGO, an offline reinforcement learning framework that realizes this separation for flow-based VLAs. A central challenge in this formulation is to learn a critic that remains grounded in logged robot experience while providing useful value signals for newly generated actions. OVOGO introduces a Return-Anchored Ranking Critic that combines in-sample distributional value learning with guarded local ranking, improving discrimination among generated actions without assigning them artificial return targets. The frozen critic then provides group-relative value signals for selected-transition optimization of fresh action candidates sampled from the current flow policy. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, DexJoCo, and LIBERO, as well as a real-robot dexterous manipulation task, show that OVOGO improves the initial VLA across all four settings and achieves higher success rates than the evaluated offline adaptation and value-guided baselines. These results suggest that offline robot experience can be repeatedly reused for value learning while inexpensive generative sampling supports policy optimization, providing an effective approach to experience-based post-training of flow-based VLAs.

papers.title_en: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
papers.authors: Haoran Zhang, Haokai Ding, Han Zhou, Zuxing Lu, Heng Zhang, Xingxing Zuo
papers.evidence: 从单次人类演示学习双手灵巧操作
papers.tldr: 人类双手演示能提供丰富灵巧技能，但迁移到机器人手时常只优化物体轨迹，忽视手物接触，导致接触错误或手指滑动。DexDuet从单次人类演示学习保持接触的双臂灵巧操作，用两种交互奖励约束手物构型与接触，并将策略分解为权重共享、互相条件化的单手策略，配合A-RSI自适应课程。三个仿真器、五种本体、四个基准上，其ADD-AUC提升11至41分，接触保持更优；122组精度相近的配对运行中117组更好保留人类接触，表明应把接触保持作为演示迁移核心。
papers.abstract_en: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation. We present DexDuet, a framework that learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterity from a single human demonstration. DexDuet employs two interaction rewards to preserve human hand-object configurations and contacts. To enable coordinated manipulation, we factorize the bimanual policy into two weight-sharing per-hand policies that condition on each other's states. We further propose assisted reference-state initialization (A-RSI), an adaptive curriculum that adjusts object assistance and training starts across demonstration segments to overcome difficult manipulation phases. Across four benchmarks spanning three simulators and five robot embodiments, DexDuet improves object-tracking ADD-AUC by 11 to 41 points over the corresponding baselines while consistently achieving better contact preservation. Notably, among 122 paired runs with comparable object-tracking accuracy, DexDuet preserves the human's contacts better in 117 cases. Code and videos are available at https://rcl-robotics.github.io/Dexduet.io/

papers.title_en: EgoSwarm: Learning Decentralized Robot Swarm Intelligence from Human Swarm Demonstrations
papers.authors: Ziqiang Liu, Xitong Chen, Min Li, Yiqun Li, Zhuoping Yin
papers.evidence: 从人类示范学习去中心化多机器人群体协同
papers.tldr: 多机器人协作需建模智能体间依赖，但个体示范监督有限，多机示范又难以规模化采集。EgoSwarm利用无机器人多人第一视角系统采集超50小时协作经验，并提出SIP与SIT从分布式观测恢复交互关系，转化为符合部署约束的局部监督。SwarmVLA将群体行为知识迁移到仅依赖局部观测、历史与有限邻居消息的去中心化策略。三类多机器人协作任务平均成功率达72.2%，为从人类群体示范学习机器人集群智能提供新框架。
papers.abstract_en: Advancing from individual embodied intelligence to swarm embodied intelligence is a key step toward scalable, general-purpose embodied intelligence. Complex tasks often require multiple agents to divide responsibilities, coordinate handovers, and manipulate shared objects collaboratively. However, existing robot learning methods rely primarily on individual demonstrations, which provide limited supervision for modeling dependencies among agent actions, while collecting multi-robot demonstrations at scale remains difficult. Human egocentric demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, yet distributed observations from multiple participants cannot directly supervise decentralized policies. We introduce EgoSwarm, the first robot learning framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations. EgoSwarm collects more than 50 hours of collaborative experience using a robot-free multi-person egocentric system. We introduce the Swarm Interaction Packet (SIP) and Swarm Interaction Token (SIT) to recover cross-agent interaction relations from distributed observations and transform this experience into local supervision consistent with deployment-time information constraints. We further propose SwarmVLA, which transfers knowledge of swarm behavior to decentralized policies conditioned on local observations, local history, and limited neighbor messages. SwarmVLA achieves a mean success rate of 72.2% across three categories of multi-robot collaborative tasks. Project page:https://xitong-c.github.io/EgoSwarm_Page/.

papers.title_en: Multi-CONDOR: Learning Multistable Motion Primitives from Demonstration
papers.authors: Gabriele Giuseppe Di Marzo, Mariano Ramírez Montero, Maximilian Stölzle, Rodrigo Pérez-Dattari, Cosimo Della Santina
papers.evidence: 通过模仿从演示学习运动基元
papers.tldr: 针对操作任务常含多个离散目标或连续可接受目标、单一稳定运动基元难以保留选择的问题，提出基于CONDOR的multi-CONDOR框架，结合模仿学习与潜参考系统一致性损失，学习多吸引子或连续吸引目标轮廓的运动动力学。方法给出Lyapunov收敛性分析，并在仿真和Franka抓取实验中验证。仿真中轨迹RMSE较状态机选择单目标基元降低约72%，双/三目标任务超出容差比例由StableNODE的0.31%和7.29%均降至0%。该工作兼顾运动复现与收敛到多种有效结果的灵活性。
papers.abstract_en: Dynamical-system-based motion policies provide a framework for learning reactive robot motions with stability and convergence properties. Many manipulation tasks, however, admit several distinct goals or a continuous set of acceptable outcomes, requiring motion primitives that preserve these alternatives. Accommodating both goal structures within a unified framework with continuous, autonomous dynamics remains an open challenge. We propose a CONDOR-based framework, multi-CONDOR, for learning motion primitives with either multiple discrete attractors or a continuous attracting goal contour. The approach combines imitation learning with losses that encourage agreement between the learned task dynamics and latent reference systems encoding the desired attraction structure. We provide a Lyapunov-based analysis of the convergence properties of the learned motion dynamics. We evaluate the framework on simulated benchmarks with discrete goals, qualitative examples with continuous goal contours, and robotic grasping experiments. In simulation, multi-CONDOR reduces trajectory RMSE by approximately 72% compared with separately learned single-goal motion primitives selected by a state machine. For tasks with two and three goals, respectively, it reduces the fraction of evaluated initial states ending outside the goal tolerance from StableNODE's 0.31% and 7.29% to 0% in both settings. Experiments with a Franka Emika robot arm demonstrate successful grasping of a container by either of its two handles using motions learned from demonstrations. Together, these results show multi-CONDOR combines motion reproduction with the flexibility to converge to alternative valid outcomes.

papers.title_en: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems
papers.authors: Saray Bakker, Wendelin Böhmer, Javier Alonso-Mora
papers.evidence: 多机器人协同的自适应学习动力学系统
papers.tldr: 针对多移动机械臂协同作业中动作协调、全身避碰与保持示范行为的问题，提出CALDS框架，将单智能体学习到的动态系统（DS）适配为协同策略。方法包含协同策略选择与时间适配，前者筛选兼容策略组合，后者在保持原行为空间结构与收敛性的同时实现无碰撞协作。在三类场景中，CALDS提升了任务成功率，并支持安全的同时执行，同时保持对示范行为的保真度。
papers.abstract_en: Cooperative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate their motions while ensuring whole-body collision avoidance and preserving task-relevant behaviors. We propose CALDS (Cooperative Adaptation of Learned Dynamical Systems), a framework that enables mobile manipulators to adapt learned single-agent behaviors for coordinated execution. Building on individual dynamical systems (DSs) learned from demonstrations, CALDS enables cooperative adaptation through two key components: Cooperative Policy Selection, which identifies compatible combinations of learned policies, and Temporal Adaptation, which ensures collision-free cooperation while preserving the spatial structure and convergence properties of the original behaviors. We evaluate CALDS across three diverse scenarios: assistive dressing, restaurant cleaning and serving, and drawer opening and object placement. Quantitative results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving task success and enabling safe, coordinated simultaneous execution while maintaining fidelity to demonstrated behaviors.

papers.title_en: From Human Videos to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Data: Confidence-Guided RL Refinement of Video Priors
papers.authors: Yanghong Liu, Yang Chen, Kailang Xu, Bang Du, Feiyang Yang, Jiawei Xia, Zhengtao Yao, Yubiao Zhang, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Ruihai Wu, Wei Zhan
papers.evidence: 利用强化学习从人类视频示范学习机器人操作
papers.tldr: 双灵巧手操作演示采集成本高，人类视频虽可提供先验，但动作估计不确定且人机具身差异大。PriDex 在仿真中用强化学习将视频先验细化为可执行机器人演示：利用交互可供性选择抓取，并以物体轨迹和双臂腕相对轨迹作为任务级与协调级参考，按物体运动置信度自适应平衡二者。在倒水、扫入簸箕、拧瓶盖和擦盘子四类任务上，方法生成机器人数据并训练视觉扩散策略。其贡献在于把不确定的人类视频先验转化为受机器人运动学与物理约束的可用操作数据。
papers.abstract_en: Collecting demonstrations for bimanual dexterous manipulation is costly, motivating the use of human videos as a source of robot training data. However, uncertainty in video-derived motion estimates and differences between human and robot embodiments make direct motion transfer challenging. In this work, we introduce PriDex, a framework that transforms human-video Priors into executable robot Dexterous manipulation demonstrations through reinforcement learning in simulation. PriDex preserves task-relevant interaction structure while allowing embodiment-specific behavior to be regenerated for the robot. Human-object interactions provide affordance cues for selecting task-relevant, robot-specific grasps from geometry-based candidates. For motion refinement, object trajectories provide a task-level reference, while relative bimanual wrist trajectories offer complementary guidance for coordinated motion. Since object-motion estimates can become unreliable under occlusion or visual ambiguity, PriDex uses object-motion confidence to adaptively balance these two priors, emphasizing object-level guidance when confidence is high and increasing the contribution of wrist-level guidance as confidence decreases. Reinforcement learning refines these video-derived priors under the robot's kinematic and physical constraints, and the resulting policies are rolled out to generate robot demonstrations for training a vision-based diffusion policy. We evaluate PriDex on four bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks, including pouring, sweeping into a dustpan, bottle-cap unscrewing, and plate cleaning, assessing both simulation-based robot data generation and downstream visuomotor policy learning.

papers.title_en: Cleanly-DINO: Efficiently Learning Visual Task Spaces for Robotics
papers.authors: Adrian Röfer, Melika Shekarriz, José Arce y de la Borbolla, Iman Nematollahi, Abhinav Valada
papers.evidence: 从示教中学习面向机器人操作感知的视觉任务空间
papers.tldr: 清洁等操作任务常由视觉状态变化而非物体位姿定义，传统任务表征难以直接适用，如何选择合适表征仍不明确。Cleanly-DINO利用任务相关区域掩码与冻结ViT特征，学习投影以分离视觉任务空间，并拟合任务进度度量。模型能从少量示范中定位未完成清洁区域，并跨视觉域迁移，还可作为强化学习观测编码器和奖励信号。研究进一步在真实机器人擦拭流程中部署，验证了其引导任务执行的实用性。
papers.abstract_en: Learning manipulation tasks from few demonstrations requires abstractions that capture the changes relevant to task completion, such as object poses in rigid-body manipulation. However, tasks such as cleaning are defined by changes in visual state rather than object pose, making the choice of task representation less clear. In this work, we propose Cleanly-DINO to learn visual task spaces from few demonstrations. Given a mask of a task-relevant region and frozen ViT features, Cleanly-DINO fits a projection to isolate a task space and fit a progression metric to it. We train the model on diverse cleaning examples and evaluate its ability to localize incomplete task regions and transfer across visual domains. We also study its utility for robot learning by using it as an observation encoder and reward signal in a reinforcement learning setting. Finally, we deploy our fitted model within a real-world robotic wiping pipeline to evaluate its use in guiding task execution.

papers.title_en: ReLAP: Latent Action Pretraining through Recurrent Video Prediction in JEPA Space
papers.authors: R. Gnana Praveen, Ali Rouzbayani, Zhiying Jiang, Bidhan Roy
papers.evidence: 面向机器人行为学习的潜在动作预训练
papers.tldr: 机器人从无动作标注视频学习控制时，潜在动作不仅要建模相邻帧局部变化，还要保持多步时序一致。ReLAP在冻结JEPA表征空间联合训练逆动力学与循环潜世界模型，让未来特征预测误差回传至早期潜在动作，并将该表征蒸馏到VLM，再用动作流匹配适配机器人。仅用11M预训练样本和1.06B可训练参数，便在LIBERO取得97.9%、LIBERO-Plus零样本扰动70.0%。部署时移除显式分支，由VLM直接输出动作，展示了无动作预训练的可迁移性与实用价值。
papers.abstract_en: Videos provide a rich source of physical interaction for learning robot behavior without action annotations, yet effective latent actions must capture not only local transitions but also how those transitions evolve over time. We introduce ReLAP, a latent-action pretraining framework that couples local transition learning with recurrent multi-step prediction in a frozen JEPA representation space. A shared inverse dynamics model infers compact continuous latent actions from adjacent observations, while a latent world model recurrently predicts the future JEPA features. Because each predicted feature becomes the context for the next transition, errors at later steps backpropagate through the rollout to earlier latent actions, encouraging temporally coherent dynamics beyond pairwise reconstruction. We transfer this representation to a vision-language model using two complementary objectives: latent distillation from the frozen inverse teacher and recurrent future-feature prediction through the frozen latent world model. The resulting policy is then adapted to robot demonstrations with action flow matching. At deployment, the explicit latent-action and world-model branches are removed, and the fine-tuned VLM predicts physical actions directly, reducing inference complexity. With only 11M pretraining samples and 1.06B trainable parameters, ReLAP achieves 97.9% on standard LIBERO and 70.0% over zero-shot LIBERO-Plus perturbations. On the LARY latent-action benchmark, ReLAP ranks second in both mean regression error and mean classification accuracy among the compared methods. These results demonstrate that recurrent action-free latent action pretraining can learn compact, temporally structured, and transferable representations for downstream robot control.

papers.title_en: Hidden Variables Behind Real-Robot Data Quality: Lessons from Hundreds of Thousands of Hours
papers.authors: Maniformer Real-World Manipulation Team, Che Tsang Calvin, Xingyu Chen, Bowen Jiang, Naixiang Gao, Xiongfeng Cai, Enlin Gu, Ruiying Li, Peize Li, Mianrui Zhu, Haomiao Zhang, Xin He, Minhui Yu, Jun Zhao, Zihao Zhu, Yang Chen, Jingmei Jin, Keru Zhou, Chen Wang, Chang Zhou, Zhiwen Hou, Di Yang, Wenjun Sun, Fan Yang, Liyan Zhang, Yi Lu, Haojun Ma, Jun Zhu, Pengxin Zha, Zhaosheng Wang, Xin Zhao, Xindong He, Chiming Liu, Jianheng Song, Jiayao Ma, Maoqing Yao, Guanghui Ren, Qian Wang, Wei Shan, Yang Yang, Li Liu, Wenhao Wang
papers.evidence: 遥操作与本体设计影响真实机器人演示数据质量
papers.tldr: 真实机器人数据规模化采集时，工作空间、遥操作接口与延迟会把停顿、绕路和修正动作带入示范。作者结合25台双臂机器人运动学分析、受控遥操作实验与π0.5策略真机评测，研究本体、控制和数据一致性。结果显示并行控制缩短任务时间43-53%，主动搜索使选臂准确率从50%升至100%，推理时标定错位令30次试验全失败。研究主张扩采前评估有效工作空间、控制效率、观测完整性、标定对齐与运动质量。
papers.abstract_en: As real-robot data collection scales, collection-system design shapes both operator efficiency and the behaviors learned by robot policies. Workspace limitations, control-interface friction, and latency can introduce pauses, detours, and corrective motions into otherwise successful demonstrations. We investigate these effects across embodiment, teleoperation control, and data consistency, combining a kinematic study of 25 dual-arm robots, controlled teleoperation experiments, and real-robot evaluation of fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policies. The embodiment study shows that positional reachability overstates orientation-aware task coverage and that modest shoulder motion can substantially expand the effective workspace. Teleoperation experiments show that parallelizing body-part control reduces task completion time by 43-53%, while compliant control improves success and reduces peak contact forces on constrained and contact-rich tasks. Policy-learning experiments show that demonstrations must capture the visual information underlying action choices: active-search demonstrations improve arm-selection accuracy from chance (50%) to 100%. Calibration experiments reveal that mixed-calibration training data remain usable in our tested configurations when an inference-aligned subset is retained, whereas inference-time miscalibration causes all 30 trials to fail. Policies also retain approximately 90% of the extra path length in detour-contaminated demonstrations, showing how inefficient operator motions persist in learned behavior. Together, these findings connect collection-system design to demonstration quality and downstream policy execution. They motivate evaluating effective workspace, control efficiency, observation completeness, calibration alignment, and motion quality before scaling collection, and addressing system-induced compensations at their source.

papers.title_en: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation
papers.authors: Baicheng Li, Wenkang Qin, Youqi Pan, Dongxiao Mao, Yukun Zhou, Chuanfu Shen, Dong Wu, Shunkai Zhou, Zike Yan, Wei Sui, Hongbin Zha
papers.evidence: 跨本体机器人演示数据的零样本组合泛化
papers.tldr: 机器人示范数据来自不同本体，导致大量机器人-技能组合缺失；合并数据虽能共享视觉知识，但关节标签绑定于演示运动链。本文提出几何监督训练框架，利用标定正运动学把示范命令转换为可执行机器人的工具空间目标，从而在无该技能关节标签时监督异体原生动作接口。视觉策略预测共享动作，并通过目标机器人原生解码器执行，同时以正可达性检查筛选跨机器人监督目标。在三类骨干和两个仿真器上的重复训练与评测表明，该方法能更好迁移到缺失的机器人-任务组合。
papers.abstract_en: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills. The central insight is that a demonstrated command provides a tool-space target for every robot that can realize it. Calibrated forward kinematics supplies this supervision to foreign native action interfaces without their joint labels for that skill. Native reconstruction retains demonstrated configurations, and positive reachability checks select targets for cross-robot supervision. A visual policy learns to predict shared actions and executes through the target robot's native decoder. During policy learning, one prediction receives geometric supervision through both source and foreign native realizations. Matched supervision controls, repeated policy training and evaluations across three backbones and two simulators demonstrate improved transfer to missing robot-task combinations.

papers.title_en: CRAFT: A Robot-Agent Harness with Scope-Aware Adaptation
papers.authors: Peng Zhang, Jiawen Wang, Cheng Xue, Jochen Renz
papers.evidence: 机器人从人类纠正反馈中学习局部放置要求
papers.tldr: 机器人能移动物体，却未必知道该放哪里；当人类拒绝一次放置时，还需判断纠正只适用于当前情境，还是应泛化为更广规则。CRAFT 在不重训机器人技能的前提下，将物理成功与需求满足分开记录，并用范围阶梯按情境记忆、显式规则和学习器加权融合来学习局部需求。仿真中，它在效用上优于仅靠纠正记忆，提问次数少于带持久记忆的语言模型智能体；但部分此类智能体错误动作更少、需求变化后成功率更高。结果表明，具体记忆与广义规则结合有价值，而变化需求下的可靠适应仍未解决。
papers.abstract_en: A robot may know how to move an object yet still need to learn where it belongs. When a person rejects a placement, the robot must decide whether the correction applies only to that situation or expresses a broader rule. We study this problem in CRAFT (Contextual Requirement Adaptation with Frozen Tools), a framework for learning local requirements without retraining robot skills. It records physical success separately from whether an action meets the requirement. Our scope ladder uses memory when an action has already been judged in a nearly identical situation. Elsewhere, it combines memory, explicit rules and a learner for requirements beyond those rules, weighting their predictions by how well they predicted earlier feedback. Controlled studies show gains over correction memory alone in utility, which rewards acceptable actions and charges for mistakes and questions. In camera-grounded robot simulations, the ladder asks fewer questions than language-model agents with persistent memory, but some of those agents take fewer wrong actions and succeed more often after requirements change. All execution failures and timeouts remain in the evaluation. These results support combining specific memories with broader rules, while leaving reliable adaptation to changing requirements unresolved. All evidence comes from simulation with generated requirements and simulated feedback.

papers.title_en: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
papers.authors: Daehee Lee, Dongsu Lee, Sanghyun Ahn, Minjong Yoo, Honguk Woo
papers.evidence: 重构程序性知识实现机器人技能适配
papers.tldr: 通用行为模型已内化大量程序性知识，面向新目标与技能接口的适应，核心在于对既有能力进行低成本重配置，而非从头学习新行为。RecPo 以多视图方式任务无关地表征技能，构建技能诱发转移的程序知识库，并在部署时用同一视图解析任务规格、对存储关系做组合查询以绑定可执行技能。在扩展 Franka Kitchen 长程任务中，它取得 91.9% 有序完成率，每回合任务推理仅 1.0 ms，且在过程支持度与任务记录稀疏度变化下保持稳定。真实机器人实验还显示，仅靠局部记忆编辑即可完成适配，无需任务特定重训练。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes. RecPo maintains a procedure knowledge base of skill-induced transitions, with each view exposing a reusable factor and preserving local skill connectivity. At deployment, it interprets task specifications through the same views and resolves the resulting compositional queries over the stored relations to bind skills for execution. On long-horizon tasks in an extended Franka Kitchen benchmark, RecPo achieves 91.9% ordered completion with 1.0 ms of task inference per episode across varying procedure support and task-record sparsity. Real-robot studies further demonstrate adaptation through local memory edits without task-specific retraining.

papers.title_en: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
papers.authors: Yuhang Huang, Junchao Li, Boyang Ma, Minghui Xu, Kaidi Xu, Pengfei Hu, Xiuzhen Cheng, Yue Zhang
papers.evidence: 用户意图与机器人动作间的跨模型错位
papers.tldr: 商用机器人依赖大语言模型理解意图，并由专用动作模型转成物理动作，形成“心智—模型协作—运动”的语义边界。该边界可能导致语义一致性断裂，使用户未显式下达动作指令时机器人仍执行非预期行为。作者提出黑盒框架TARS，自动探索命令—推理—动作链路并发现、验证此类失配。在四款商用机器人44种设置、133400次执行中，TARS揭示广泛存在的跨模型动作失配，验证动作覆盖率达94%。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied robots increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction. This multi-model pipeline creates a critical semantic boundary across mind, model collaboration, and motion: semantic consistency may break between what the large model understands, how the small action model translates that understanding into executable commands, and what physical actions the robot ultimately performs. As a security consequence, commercial robots may execute unintended physical actions even when user inputs contain no explicit action commands. To measure this problem, we develop TARS, a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors. We evaluate TARS on four commercial robots across 44 experimental settings, conducting 133,400 executions. TARS uncovers widespread cross-model action misalignment and achieves up to 94% verified action coverage.
